heading.en: Everyone moves on the same beat

hook.en: In a ripple counter the flip-flops change one after another, like dominoes falling. In a *synchronous* counter all of them hear the same clock and change together, like soldiers marching.

title.en: Explain a 3-bit and 4-bit synchronous binary counter
Write the J and K input conditions for each stage

say.en: In a ripple counter the flip-flops change one after another, like dominoes falling. In a synchronous counter all of them hear the same clock and change together, like soldiers marching. In this lesson: Explain a 3-bit and 4-bit synchronous binary counter.
Write the J and K input conditions for each stage.
Compare synchronous and asynchronous counters.

body.en: In a *synchronous* counter every flip-flop receives the same clock, so all of them change at the same instant. Gates decide which flip-flops toggle. In binary counting a bit toggles when all the lower bits are 1, so with JK flip-flops: $J_0 = K_0 = 1$, $J_1 = K_1 = Q_0$, $J_2 = K_2 = Q_0Q_1$ and $J_3 = K_3 = Q_0Q_1Q_2$. Synchronous counter ICs include 74160–74163 and the up/down counters 74190–74193.

points.en: A bit toggles when all lower bits are 1

narration.en: In a synchronous counter all flip-flops share one clock. A stage toggles only when all the lower bits are one, so its J and K come from an AND of those outputs.
narration.kn: ಸಮಕಾಲಿಕ ಕೌಂಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲ ಫ್ಲಿಪ್-ಫ್ಲಾಪ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಕ್ಲಾಕ್. ಕೆಳಗಿನ ಎಲ್ಲ ಬಿಟ್‌ಗಳು 1 ಆದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಒಂದು ಹಂತ ಟಾಗಲ್ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಅದರ J, K ಆ ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್‌ಗಳ AND.

body.en: A ripple counter is simple (no extra gates) but slow: the delays of all stages add, $f_{max} \approx 1/(n\,t_{pd})$, and false intermediate states (glitches) appear while the carry ripples. A *synchronous* counter needs extra AND gates but all outputs settle after one flip-flop delay plus one gate delay, so $f_{max} \approx 1/(t_{pd} + t_{AND})$, independent of n, with no ripple glitches. Synchronous counters are used in fast digital systems, frequency counters and digital clocks.

points.en: *Synchronous*: extra gates, fast, no ripple glitches

problem.en: A 4-bit synchronous up counter is in state Q3Q2Q1Q0 = 0111. Which flip-flops toggle on the next clock, and what is the next state?

steps.en: Q0 = 1 → Q1 toggles; Q0Q1 = 1 → Q2 toggles.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A 4-bit synchronous up counter is in state Q3Q2Q1Q0 = 0111. Which flip-flops toggle on the next clock, and what is the next state?

say.en: Let us work this out together. A 4-bit synchronous up counter is in state Q3Q2Q1Q0 equals 0111. Which flip-flops toggle on the next clock, and what is the next state?
J0 equals K0 equals 1 gives Q0 toggles.
Q0 equals 1 gives Q1 toggles; Q0Q1 equals 1 gives Q2 toggles.
Q0Q1Q2 equals 1 gives Q3 toggles.
All four toggle: 0111 gives 1000.
So the answer is All four toggle; next state 1000.

problem.en: Flip-flops have tpd = 20 ns and AND gates 10 ns. Compare the maximum clock frequency of 4-bit ripple and synchronous counters.

steps.en: Ripple: n × tpd = 4 × 20 = 80 ns → f_max = 1/80 ns = 12.5 MHz.
Synchronous: tpd + tAND = 20 + 10 = 30 ns → f_max = 1/30 ns ≈ 33.3 MHz.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Flip-flops have tpd = 20 ns and AND gates 10 ns. Compare the maximum clock frequency of 4-bit ripple and synchronous counters.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Flip-flops have tpd equals 20 ns and AND gates 10 ns. Compare the maximum clock frequency of 4-bit ripple and synchronous counters.
Ripple: n times tpd equals 4 times 20 equals 80 ns gives f max equals 1 over 80 ns equals 12.5 megahertz.
Synchronous: tpd plus tAND equals 20 plus 10 equals 30 ns gives f max equals 1 over 30 ns is approximately 33.3 megahertz.
So the answer is Ripple 12.5 megahertz; synchronous is approximately 33.3 megahertz.
